title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Company Personnel
tiers.description: All Directors and Senior Management, employees of Viva Energy (permanent, fixed-term, casual or temporary) and Affected Parties. Subject only to the insider trading prohibition in section 3; the trading window, clearance, protection arrangement, margin lending and speculative trading restrictions bite only on Designated Persons.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All Directors and Senior Management and any other person designated as a Designated Person by the Board and/or Company Secretary from time to time. Bears every additional restriction: dealing only in a Trading Window and only with clearance, the section 5.1 speculative trading ban, the section 5.2 protection arrangements regime and the section 5.3 margin lending prohibition, and must procure compliance by their Affected Parties.

tiers.name: Directors and Senior Management
tiers.description: Each director of the Company, the Company Secretary, the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer and Key Management Personnel of Viva Energy. Distinguished only for clearance: the chair of the Board is their Authorising Officer. Directors additionally have a three business day notification duty to the Company Secretary for ASX notifiable interest changes.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The chair of the Board, whose Authorising Officer and exceptional-circumstances Clearance Officer is the chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Affected Parties
tiers.description: Immediate family members living with a Designated Person and other immediate family members whose investment decisions the Designated Person controls; any company, trust, managed superannuation fund or other entity controlled by the Designated Person or such a family member; and, for directors only, any person or entity whose dealing would require the director's disclosure to ASX, including where the director controls the right to vote or dispose of Company securities or is entitled to benefit from a contract to call for or deliver Company securities.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which: (c) amount to 'short selling' of securities beyond the relevant person's holding of securities; (d) operate to limit the economic risk of the relevant person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including the Company's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that person's behalf; or (e) otherwise enable the relevant person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.

windows.start_anchor: commencement of trading on ASX on the trading day following release of the Company's half year results
commencement of trading on ASX on the trading day following release of the Company's full year results
commencement of trading on ASX on the trading day following release of the Company's first quarter update
commencement of trading on ASX on the trading day following release of the Company's third quarter update
any other period that the Board specifies from time to time

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may impose additional restrictions on dealing by any or all Designated Persons and their Affected Parties, even where the dealing would otherwise be permitted in a Trading Window. Any such restriction must be kept confidential by the Designated Person, who may pass it to affected Affected Parties on the same confidential basis.

rules.detail: Derivatives over Company securities are addressed as 'Company products in the derivatives markets' within the protection arrangements regime. Over vested, unrestricted shares a put and call are permitted but require approval under section 4.3(a): notification of the type of dealing and number of securities, confirmation of no Inside Information, written consent from the Authorising Officer, execution within five clear trading days, and a post-trade transaction confirmation. Dealing is confined to a four-week Trading Window unless the Clearance Officer grants exceptional-circumstances clearance. No venue distinction is drawn, so OTC legs with a bank are treated the same as listed options.
rules.evidence: The entering by a Designated Person or their Affected Parties into all types of "protection arrangements" for any of the Company's securities (or Company products in the derivatives markets): ... (b) otherwise, requires approval under section 4.3(a).

rules.detail: Derivative protection arrangements over unvested Company securities are banned at any time with no approval route.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: Employees who are not Designated Persons are subject only to the insider trading prohibition; the Trading Window, clearance, protection arrangement and margin lending rules in sections 4 and 5 are expressly framed as additional restrictions on Designated Persons and their Affected Parties.
rules.evidence: Additional restrictions are imposed on Designated Persons and their Affected Parties when dealing in the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Arrangements limiting the economic risk of unvested Company securities are prohibited at any time, with no approval route. The ban expressly reaches securities held beneficially on the person's behalf, including under an incentive plan or in trust.
rules.evidence: The entering by a Designated Person or their Affected Parties into all types of "protection arrangements" for any of the Company's securities ... is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: Securities subject to a holding lock are treated identically to unvested securities: hedging them is prohibited at any time regardless of vesting, so post-vesting restricted shares cannot form part of the collared parcel.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: For vested shares free of a holding lock the policy does not prohibit hedging; it channels it into the ordinary clearance process. The hedge must be approved by the Authorising Officer, executed within five clear trading days, entered inside a Trading Window (or with exceptional-circumstances clearance), and confirmed to the Authorising Officer afterwards. Section 5.1's ban on short-term or speculative derivative transactions still constrains tenor.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of the relevant person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) ... otherwise, requires approval under section 4.3(a).

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan both limits economic risk and enables the person to profit from a decrease in the market price, so it is a protection arrangement: prohibited over unvested or holding-locked securities and otherwise requiring approval under section 4.3(a). The accompanying loan is separately constrained by the margin lending prohibition in section 5.3 if it has margin lending characteristics.
rules.evidence: otherwise enable the relevant person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.

rules.floor: the relevant person's holding of securities
rules.detail: Short selling is dealt with only as a species of protection arrangement: transactions that amount to short selling beyond the person's holding are prohibited over unvested or holding-locked securities and otherwise require approval under section 4.3(a). Read with section 5.1, which says Designated Persons should under no circumstances engage in speculative trading, a naked short would in practice be refused. A covered collar written against shares actually held does not exceed the holding and so is not short selling for this purpose.
rules.evidence: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which: (c) amount to "short selling" of securities beyond the relevant person's holding of securities;

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and no definition sweeps it in. A lend transferring title would change the beneficial interest and so fall outside the section 6(a)(i) exemption, making it a dealing that needs a Trading Window and clearance.

Contracts for difference are named as an example of derivative market transactions caught by the absolute ban on short-term or speculative trading. A CFD that was neither short-term nor speculative would still be a protection arrangement under section 5.2 if it limited economic risk or allowed profit from a price fall, and so would be prohibited over unvested or locked securities and need approval otherwise.
rules.evidence: This prohibition includes short-term direct dealing in the Company's securities (within a period of less than three months) as well as transactions in the derivative markets (including exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference and other similar instruments) which are short-term or speculative.

rules.detail: Absolute ban at any time, direct or indirect, on entering into any margin lending arrangement involving Company securities, extending to Affected Parties whom the Designated Person must procure to comply. Entering the arrangement, transferring Company securities into an existing margin loan account and selling Company securities to satisfy a margin call are each given as prohibited examples. There is no approval or exceptional-circumstances route.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not at any time, and must procure that their Affected Parties do not at any time, directly or indirectly, enter into any margin lending arrangement involving the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge or a pledge over Company securities is not itself defined as a dealing and is prohibited only where it forms part of a margin lending arrangement. The exemption for disposals resulting from a secured lender exercising rights 'under a loan or security agreement' shows the policy contemplates Designated Persons pledging shares under a non-margin secured facility without that pledge being banned.

There is no general ban on secured financing; only margin lending arrangements are prohibited. Section 6(a)(vii) expressly exempts a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement, which presupposes that a Designated Person may have granted security over Company securities under a non-margin facility. The risk is characterisation: a facility with an LVR, margin call or top-up mechanic over Company securities would be an indirect margin lending arrangement and so prohibited.
rules.evidence: dispose of Company securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement;

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition, with no approval route, on short-term or speculative trading: direct dealing within a period of less than three months, and short-term or speculative transactions in the derivative markets including exchange traded options, share warrants and CFDs. Tenor and speculative character are therefore a live constraint on the derivative legs of any structure.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons or their Affected Parties engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's securities.

clearance.approver: The chair of the Board, who shall where appropriate consult with the Chief Executive Officer and the Company Secretary (other than where they are the Designated Person). All requests and responses must be copied to the Company Secretary for record keeping
clearance.post_trade_to: Authorising Officer (transaction confirmation); directors must also notify the Company Secretary in writing of ASX notifiable interest changes
clearance.post_trade_deadline: transaction confirmation after the dealing (no deadline stated); directors immediately and no later than 3 business days after any relevant event for ASX notification purposes
clearance.evidence: obtain written consent from the Authorising Officer (which may be given by email) confirming that there is no known reason to preclude the dealing in Company securities; order or otherwise authorise the dealing in Company securities within five clear trading days of receiving approval

clearance.approver: The chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, who shall where appropriate consult with the Chief Executive Officer and the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_to: Authorising Officer (transaction confirmation); Company Secretary for ASX notifiable interest changes
clearance.post_trade_deadline: transaction confirmation after the dealing; no later than 3 business days after any relevant event for ASX notification
clearance.evidence: Chair of the Board - The chair of the Audit and Risk Committee. The chair of the Audit and Risk Committee shall, where appropriate, consult with the Chief Executive Officer and the Company Secretary.

clearance.approver: The Company Secretary, who shall where appropriate consult with the Chief Executive Officer, for any Designated Person other than Directors and Senior Management
clearance.post_trade_deadline: after the dealing; no deadline stated
clearance.evidence: clearance can be given or refused at the discretion of the Authorising Officer, without giving reasons; clearance can be withdrawn by the Authorising Officer at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised, if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances;
Additional restrictions are imposed on Designated Persons and their Affected Parties when dealing in the Company's securities.

short_term.basis: direct dealing within a period of less than three months; also captures short-term or speculative derivative market transactions
short_term.evidence: This prohibition includes short-term direct dealing in the Company's securities (within a period of less than three months) as well as transactions in the derivative markets (including exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference and other similar instruments) which are short-term or speculative.

exceptions.approver: Must advise the relevant Authorising Officer after the event
exceptions.evidence: deal in the Company's securities where the dealing does not result in a change of beneficial interest in the securities;

exceptions.approver: Must advise the relevant Authorising Officer after the event
exceptions.evidence: acquire securities under any director or employee security plan or through the exercise of options or performance rights under an option or performance rights plan or acquire, or agree to acquire, options or performance rights under an option or performance rights plan;

acquire the Company's ordinary shares by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to the Company's ordinary shares; acquire the Company's securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class;
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer;

invest in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party;

exceptions.approver: Must advise the relevant Authorising Officer after the event
exceptions.evidence: dispose of Company securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement;

exceptions.approver: Board approves the plan determining the timing and structure of the offer
exceptions.evidence: deal under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan or an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.
transfer Company securities already held into a self-managed superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Designated Person or the Affected Party (as applicable) is a beneficiary;

exceptions.approver: Decision taken by the other trustees or investment managers independently
exceptions.evidence: where a Designated Person or an Affected Party is a trustee, deal in the securities managed by that trust provided the Designated Person or the Affected Party (as applicable) is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to deal during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently

exceptions.approver: The chair of the Board as Clearance Officer, or the chair of the Audit and Risk Committee where the chair of the Board is the applicant
exceptions.evidence: What constitutes "exceptional circumstances" will be assessed on a case-by-case basis within the absolute discretion of the Clearance Officer, and may include, without limitation, severe financial hardship or a requirement to comply with a court order or court enforceable undertaking.

exceptions.approver: Clearance Officer (chair of the Board, or chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the chair)
exceptions.evidence: a requirement to comply with a court order or court enforceable undertaking.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No guidance on trigger levels. Selling Company securities to satisfy a margin call is listed as an example of a prohibited margin lending dealing rather than something that can be cleared, whereas a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights under a loan or security agreement is an outright exemption available at any time, subject only to advising the Authorising Officer afterwards.
financing_disclosure: Designated Persons: after relying on any section 6 exemption (including a secured lender's enforcement sale), the Designated Person must advise the relevant Authorising Officer; no deadline stated.

Directors: must notify the Company Secretary in writing immediately and no later than 3 business days after any relevant event, so that the Company can notify ASX of a change to notifiable interests within 5 business days.
Designated Persons: the Company Secretary or delegate maintains a copy of all approval requests and details of all dealings by Designated Persons and their Affected Parties.

exemption_authority: The chair of the Board, or where the chair is the applicant the chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, acts as Clearance Officer and may in exceptional circumstances (assessed in absolute discretion, and which may include severe financial hardship or compliance with a court order or court enforceable undertaking) clear a dealing outside a Trading Window; approval must be given by email, the section 4.3(a) notification steps still apply, the clearance may be withdrawn, and it must be kept confidential. There is no power to waive the section 5.3 margin lending prohibition, the section 5.1 speculative trading ban or the section 5.2(a) ban on protection arrangements over unvested or holding-locked securities. Amendment of the Policy requires Board approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The entering by a Designated Person or their Affected Parties into all types of "protection arrangements" for any of the Company's securities (or Company products in the derivatives markets): (a) is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and (b) otherwise, requires approval under section 4.3(a).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a two-tier regime rather than a blanket hedging ban: the collar is available over vested unrestricted shares with Authorising Officer approval, but can never touch unvested or holding-locked stock.

bespoke_clauses.clause: operate to limit the economic risk of the relevant person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including the Company's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that person's behalf
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares sitting in an employee share trust are within the protection arrangement definition, so the collar cannot be run over trust-held plan shares while they remain unvested or locked.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not at any time, and must procure that their Affected Parties do not at any time, directly or indirectly, enter into any margin lending arrangement involving the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The word 'indirectly' means a loan documented as something other than a margin loan but carrying LVR, margin call or top-up mechanics over the collared shares would be prohibited, so the funding leg must be a genuinely non-margin term facility.

bespoke_clauses.clause: dispose of Company securities that are the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The exemption confirms that non-margin secured lending against Company securities is contemplated and is not caught by section 5.3, and that the bank's enforcement sale may occur at any time, including outside a Trading Window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons or their Affected Parties engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's securities. This prohibition includes short-term direct dealing ... (within a period of less than three months) as well as transactions in the derivative markets ... which are short-term or speculative.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no approval route around this, so the collar must be long-dated and defensively characterised as risk management of an existing holding rather than a speculative derivative position.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons and their Affected Parties are only permitted to buy or sell, or otherwise deal in, Company securities: during a Trading Window; and if they have received clearance in accordance with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a positive-permission regime with only four four-week windows a year, so entry, any roll and any unwind of the collar must each be timed into a window or need exceptional-circumstances clearance from the chair.

bespoke_clauses.clause: order or otherwise authorise the dealing in Company securities within five clear trading days of receiving approval from the Authorising Officer ... if the approval is given during or after trading on one day, the order for the dealing must be lodged or otherwise authorised ... before the close of trading on the fifth trading day after the approval is given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both derivative legs and the associated share transfer must be authorised inside a tightly defined five trading day window from approval, which constrains documentation and pricing timetables.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Company may impose such restrictions notwithstanding that the dealing in the Company's securities may otherwise be permitted under section 4.1. Any restriction communicated by the Company to any or all Designated Persons under this section 4.2 must be kept confidential
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undisclosed company-imposed restriction can block entry, roll or unwind of the collar even inside a Trading Window, and the executive cannot tell the bank why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance can be given or refused at the discretion of the Authorising Officer, without giving reasons; clearance can be withdrawn by the Authorising Officer at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval is not a bankable condition precedent: it can be revoked at any point before the trade is authorised and no reason need be given.

bespoke_clauses.clause: in relation to directors of the Company only, any other person or entity where dealing in securities of the Company by that person or entity would require disclosure to the ASX by the director. This includes where the director ... is entitled to benefit from a contract to call for or deliver securities in the Company;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director's rights under the collar are themselves a contract to call for or deliver Company securities, which points to the arrangement being a notifiable interest change requiring ASX disclosure within five business days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary (or a delegate) will maintain a copy of: all requests for an approval to deal in the Company's securities submitted by a Designated Person; and details of all dealings in the Company's securities by a Designated Person and their Affected Parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The full collar and its lifecycle will sit on the company's register, so the structure cannot be kept off the company's books.

summary: A funded collar is possible for a Viva Energy Designated Person, but only over vested shares free of any holding lock and on tight timing conditions. Section 5.2 treats the put and call as 'protection arrangements': prohibited outright at any time over unvested or holding-locked securities, including plan shares held beneficially in trust, but otherwise permitted with approval under section 4.3(a) from the chair of the Board (Directors and Senior Management), the chair of the Audit and Risk Committee (the chair of the Board) or the Company Secretary (other Designated Persons), with execution within five clear trading days and a post-trade confirmation. Dealing is confined to the four four-week Trading Windows following the half year, full year and first and third quarter releases, subject to confidential ad hoc restrictions and to exceptional-circumstances clearance from the Clearance Officer, and section 5.1's absolute ban on short-term or speculative trading (under three months, and short-term or speculative derivative market transactions) means the collar must be long-dated and framed as risk management rather than speculation. The loan leg is the sharper risk: section 5.3 bans directly or indirectly entering into any margin lending arrangement involving Company securities with no approval route, so the facility must be a genuine term loan without LVR, margin call or top-up mechanics, although section 6(a)(vii) confirms that secured lending under a loan or security agreement is contemplated and that the bank's enforcement sale is exempt and may occur at any time. Directors should also expect the arrangement to be a notifiable interest change requiring ASX disclosure, since the Affected Party definition reaches contracts to call for or deliver Company securities.
